stem: An adult with an unknown tetanus vaccination history has a deep puncture wound contaminated with soil. Which prophylaxis is indicated?

options.A: Provide wound care, a tetanus toxoid-containing vaccine, and TIG 250 IU IM.
options.B: Provide wound care and tetanus vaccine without TIG because immune globulin is reserved for clean minor wounds.
options.C: Provide wound care and TIG without tetanus vaccine because passive antibody provides sufficient long-term protection.
options.D: Provide wound care and systemic antibiotics without tetanus vaccine or TIG because wound treatment prevents tetanus by itself.

rationale: CDC classifies penetrating or puncture wounds and wounds containing soil as dirty or major wounds. Tetanus vaccination is recommended for people with unknown vaccination history for all wound types, and TIG is indicated for dirty or major wounds when vaccination history is unknown. When TIG is indicated, CDC recommends 250 international units intramuscularly. Antibiotics are not recommended to prevent tetanus after a wound exposure. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: For a dirty or major wound in a person with unknown tetanus vaccination history, provide appropriate wound care, a tetanus toxoid-containing vaccine, and TIG 250 IU IM.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Clinical Guidance for Wound Management to Prevent Tetanus
source_locator: Wound assessment and care > dirty or major wounds include penetrating/puncture wounds and wounds containing dirt/soil; Vaccination recommended > For all wounds > unknown vaccination history; TIG prophylaxis indications > For dirty or major wounds > unknown vaccination history; Care > administer 250 international units of TIG intramuscularly; Antibiotic prophylaxis against tetanus isn't recommended.
source_claim_supported: A soil-contaminated puncture wound is a dirty/major wound; with unknown tetanus vaccination history, CDC recommends tetanus vaccination plus TIG, with TIG 250 IU IM when indicated.

source_original.stem: An adult with an unknown tetanus vaccination history has a deep puncture wound contaminated with soil. Which prophylaxis is indicated?

options.A: Provide wound care, tetanus vaccination, and TIG 250 IU IM because a dirty puncture wound plus unknown vaccination history requires active and passive prophylaxis.
options.B: Provide wound care and tetanus vaccine without TIG because immune globulin is reserved for clean minor wounds with incomplete vaccination.
options.C: Provide wound care and TIG without tetanus vaccine because passive antibody provides sufficient long-term protection after this exposure.
options.D: Provide wound care and systemic antibiotics without tetanus vaccine or TIG because thorough wound treatment prevents tetanus by itself.

source_original.rationale: CDC classifies penetrating or puncture wounds as dirty/major wounds. For people with unknown vaccination history, tetanus vaccination is recommended for all wounds and TIG is indicated for dirty/major wounds; the prophylactic TIG dose is 250 IU IM.
source_original.source_detail: Recommendations > Vaccination recommended > For all wounds; TIG prophylaxis indications > For dirty or major wounds; Care > TIG dose 250 IU IM. correction_summary: Retained the CDC-supported construct and key A, simplified the keyed option to avoid answer-length cueing, explicitly named a tetanus toxoid-containing vaccine, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium because the final item applies a direct CDC wound-prophylaxis algorithm.

audit_findings.claim_audit: Every final clinical claim is directly supported by current CDC guidance; no unsupported antibiotic, timing, or immunity claim remains.

distractor_audit.A: Correct: wound care plus active vaccination plus passive TIG is indicated.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect: TIG is not reserved for clean/minor wounds; it is never indicated for clean/minor wounds and is indicated here.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect: TIG provides temporary passive protection and does not replace indicated active vaccination.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect: antibiotics are not recommended as tetanus prophylaxis and cannot replace vaccination/TIG when indicated.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A satisfies both active and passive prophylaxis requirements for a dirty/major wound with unknown vaccination history.
audit_findings.cueing: Options are parallel management strategies; the keyed option was shortened to reduce length cueing.
